requirements.requirement: An SSH certificate authority is created on node1
requirements.summary: An ed25519 CA keypair was generated at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca on node1 (fingerprint SHA256:FDxAqqRfoJsRTqDdLglWTUvXfIkbNkve7fJVCKJleDo).

requirements.requirement: The host's SSH key is signed by the CA as a valid host certificate
requirements.summary: ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub was signed with -h (host cert) and principals node1,10.100.93.10, producing ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub; ssh-keygen -Lf confirms it is a host certificate signed by the created CA.

requirements.requirement: sshd on node1 is configured to present the certificate to clients
requirements.summary: HostCertificate directive was added to sshd_config, sshd -t passed, and sshd was reloaded and confirmed active.

requirements.requirement: A client trusting only the CA (no pinned host key) connects successfully under strict host key checking
requirements.summary: A client configured with only an @cert-authority line for the CA (no host-key pin) connected successfully with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes; a control test with no CA trust failed host key verification, confirming CA trust enabled the connection.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovered service/certificate/trust state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (73bafeef...) and healthy sshd/certificate state were captured; shutdown -r now returned an acknowledgement before disconnect; polling showed connection timeouts during the transition; post-restart boot_id (15ef0089...) differs from pre-restart, matching the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot; sshd, the certificate, and sshd_config directive were confirmed intact, and a fresh CA-trust-only client reconnected successfully post-restart.

overall_summary: The executor created an SSH host CA on node1, signed the ed25519 host key as a host certificate, configured and reloaded sshd to present it, and directly demonstrated (with a falsification control) that a client trusting only the CA connects under strict host key checking without any pinned host key. The separate node-restart evidence protocol was fully and coherently demonstrated: pre-restart healthy baseline, an acknowledged reboot, an observed unreachable window, a changed boot identity consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and confirmed post-restart recovery of sshd, the certificate, and CA-trust connectivity. The only hygiene concern is a leftover authorized_keys entry (CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY) added to enable the client test but never removed.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) in both lifecycle snapshots, so package-manager consistency around the reboot could not be independently cross-checked.

The added CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY entry in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys was not explicitly confirmed as removed or retained by design; treated here as residue lowering hygiene since no cleanup command targeting it was observed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map cleanly to the task or the restart protocol: CA generation, host-cert signing, sshd_config edit, sshd reload, and the pre/post-restart reboot itself are all justified and left in an intact, non-conflicting final state (confirmed by the after_executor snapshot showing no failed services, consistent listening sockets, and a matching new boot_id). Temporary client key/known_hosts files created for the CA-trust verification test were removed (cmd-5963e2ce568f468a partially failed on one file due to permission, corrected immediately by cmd-56ab7d2c8c014f88 as root), and the post-restart test client files were cleaned up inline in cmd-36e995337e9040fe. The one unresolved item is cmd-e2496d62ba6c44d9, which appended CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY as a second key in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on node1 to enable the client-side verification test; this key was never removed and persists as residue after task completion, a bounded but retained credential addition not required by the certificate-authority task itself.
